title: web-chat MCP tool catalogue: the shape of a catalogue document (contract 10)
description: The shape of a catalogue document: the 24 tools a chat's Claude Code session loads from web-chat's stdio MCP server, verbatim, with the daemon route each handler calls. Derived from web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/mcp/index.js (registration order) and lib/mcp/tools/*.js, read at a9c22e5c and re-read at 826442d6 and aa60492e; at aa60492e lib/mcp differs from tag ae-alpha.2 only by U419's get_comments and reply_comment descriptions. This schema validates shape only: each released catalogue version is its own file schemas/10-mcp-catalogue-<version>.json holding one const over the whole document, added at its release; 12's version table (C-12.6a) names the files for the versions through 0.9.0-alpha.3, and every minted file names its first web-chat package version in web_chat_from (C-10.1, C-10.9). Non-ASCII characters in descriptions are JSON escapes, so a catalogue file holds no literal em dash while every parsed string equals the source. $defs input_<name> repeat the pre-catalogue placeholder's inputSchemas, informative, for validating a call's arguments. Contract 10, C-10.1 to C-10.9.

catalogue_version.description: Semver of the catalogue; major 1 for the v1 round. Minor and patch rise by C-10.9. 1.0.0-pre is the pre-catalogue placeholder of 0.9.0-alpha.2 and alpha.2.1 (examples/10-mcp-tools.json), which no hub claims; catalogue 1.0.0 is minted at 0.9.0-alpha.3's cut.

web_chat_from.description: The first web-chat package version that carries this catalogue (0.9.0-alpha.3 for 1.0.0), in the form of 12's $defs/package_version. Optional in this shape and present in every minted catalogue file; the pre-catalogue placeholder has none. The hub maps a package version after 0.9.0-alpha.3 to the minted file with the highest web_chat_from it reaches, by compareVersions (lib/core/versions.js); 12's table (C-12.6a) covers the versions through 0.9.0-alpha.3 only, so a release that changes the catalogue adds a file, never a row (C-10.1).

registration.description: The file that registers the tools, in order.

build.description: The released build that carries this catalogue.

transport.description: How Claude reaches the tools and how the tools reach the daemon.

client_headers.description: Headers every daemon request from the MCP server carries.

catalogue_sha256.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8, RFC 8785 for these values) of [{name, description, inputSchema}] in registration order: what tools/list answers. lib/core/stable-json.js stableStringify gives the same bytes. A released version's value is the const in its schemas/10-mcp-catalogue-<version>.json. From alpha.4 web-chat commits it as CATALOGUE_SHA256 in lib/core/versions.js and GET /api/health reports it as catalogue.sha256; the hub trusts a report only when it equals a known file's value (C-10.8).

route.description: One daemon request a tool's handler makes. Derived by running each handler in web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/mcp/tools/ with lib/mcp/client.js stubbed, and checked by reading the handler.

when.description: The arguments under which the handler makes this request; 'always' when it makes it on every call.

path.description: The daemon route, Express style (:name is one encoded path segment).

query.description: Query keys the handler may set.

body.description: What the request body carries, in words; null for a GET.

timeout_ms.description: A socket timeout the handler sets; null for lib/client's default (none).

portal_v12.description: What web-chat's remote table (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/core/remote-policy.js classify, PORTAL_PROTOCOL_VERSION 12) answers for this route from a remote viewer. Informative: C-10.3 keeps tool routes off the relay whatever the verdict.

verdict.description: allowed: the portal proxies it (subject to `need`); refused: never proxied.

rule.description: The table row that decided, as keyOf() prints it.

need.description: The least mirror level the row needs, when it names one.

note.description: A body-level or query-level rule recorded beside the row.

tool.description: One MCP tool as Claude Code's tools/list sees it (name, description, inputSchema) plus where it comes from and what it calls.

source.description: The module that defines it, cited by repo path.

description.description: The tool description, verbatim. Load-bearing: Claude decides from it.

inputSchema.description: The tool's inputSchema, verbatim. It is web-chat's, so it does not follow this folder's additionalProperties and every-property-described rules.

description_sha256.description: sha256 of the description's UTF-8 bytes, so a one-word edit is visible.

routes.description: The daemon requests the handler makes.

shaping.description: What the handler changes in the daemon's answer before Claude sees it; null when the answer passes as one JSON text item.

content.description: The MCP content item types a successful result may hold.

client_header.description: A header lib/mcp/client.js adds to every daemon request from the MCP server process (and only from it).

source.description: Where the name and value are defined.

call_result.description: The CallToolResult shapes lib/mcp/index.js answers, for every tool. Normative for the hub only in that a connector MUST NOT rewrite them (C-10.2).

oneOf.title: success
oneOf.description: A handler's result as one JSON text item, or MCP content the handler built (isContentResult). A newer-build notice may lead as its own text item (lib/mcp/skew.js createBuildNotice).

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: A thrown handler error ('Error: <message>', or lib/mcp/skew.js unknownRouteError for a route the daemon lacks), an unknown tool ('Unknown tool: <name>'), or the disabled envelope as JSON text.

content_item.description: One MCP content item (text or image as web-chat emits them).

data.description: For an image item: base64 bytes.

mimeType.description: For an image item: e.g. image/png.

disabled.description: The JSON the disabled envelope's text item holds when web-chat is toggled off (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/mcp/index.js CallToolRequestSchema handler).

scope.description: The toggle scope that decided (session scope is not visible to MCP).

reason.description: not-installed: no .web-chat/ in the root; marker: someone switched it off.

html.description: The HTML/JS payload. <style> and <script> tags inside are handled correctly.

id.description: Stable mount id (used for replace-in-place). If omitted, a unique id is generated. The shell's own element ids are RESERVED — "main", "topbar", "status", "dock", "stage", "overlay", "drawer", "minbar", "queue-rail", "cmd-palette" and the rest of the chrome — and a render naming one is refused with {ok:false, reserved:true, hint}. Prefix your ids (e.g. "plan-form") and this never comes up.

target.description: Slot in the page DOM to mount into. Defaults to "main".

force.description: Take over a pane owned by another writer (owner:"service:<name>" or "pane:<id>"). Without it, rendering over an owned pane soft-rejects with {ok:false, owned:true, owner}.

after.description: Position in the page sequence: place the pane right after this pane/markdown id, or "start" for the top. Omitted: a new pane appends and a re-render keeps its position. An unknown id still mounts (appended) and returns a `warning`. Pair with `write_markdown` to put headings and prose between runs of panes.

place.description: Proposed grid placement on the page's 12-column grid: `col` (1–12, the column it starts in; omit for auto flow), `span` (2–12 columns wide, shrunk to fit right of `col`; default the rest of the row), `rows` (2–24 rows of 40px; omit for auto height). Out-of-range values are clamped and the applied placement comes back as `place`. It also becomes this pane's "Claude's layout" baseline — the user can rearrange freely and ↺ puts the run back. Omitted: a new pane is full-width auto-height and a re-render keeps whatever layout the user left.

params.description: Mount params persisted with the pane and injected into its script as `params`. Recognized keys: `title` labels the pane's header (otherwise it shows the mount id) and `type` adds a type chip beside it; `form_reset:true` drops the mount's persisted form_state on this render (use when supplying fresh prefills); `routing:"none"` opts the pane out of default activity-item routing ("auto" opts a service-owned pane back in). Other keys pass through to the pane script.

form_reset.description: Drop the persisted form_state for this mount on this render.

routing.description: Activity-routing override for this pane. Default: auto (none for service-owned panes).

signals.description: Optional declared wake signals (channels). Each entry names a store key this pane writes on a deliberate user action and how it should wake you: wake:"queue" (default) folds a browser write to that key into the user's queue rail, to send when they hit Push; wake:"immediate" wakes you the moment the pane writes it, bypassing the queue. Use "immediate" only for explicit "Ask Claude now" affordances. Declaring signals is the channels-native replacement for the arm-a-wait convention — you no longer need to background a watch for these keys.

key.description: The store key the pane writes (e.g. "form_submit").

why.description: Short human label for why this wakes you (shown in the queue rail).

target.description: Clear all mounts in this target slot.

force.description: Clear panes owned by another writer (a driver, or a parent pane) too. Without it, a clear that would take one is soft-rejected. On a bulk clear it also removes pinned panes.

name.description: kebab-case component name (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`) — it becomes a directory name. Builtin names are reserved and refused.

source.description: HTML/JS source. Scripts inside can read `params` (passed by `use_component`).

description.description: When/why to use this component. Critical for later discovery.

params_schema.description: JSON Schema for the params object the component expects.

seed.description: Optional seed.js source: a browser-side script run to compute default params when the component is mounted from the drawer.

service.description: Optional service.js host-side source. Presence makes this a service-backed component. Must `module.exports = { async start(ctx), async stop?() }`; ctx = { driver, params, mountId, name, log }. In v1 the service writes the store only (ctx.driver.setStore(...)) — no render. The daemon spawns it while its pane is on the active node and stops it when you navigate away or clear the pane.

location.description: local = this project (.web-chat/components); system = ~/.web-chat/components (all projects). Defaults to local.

params.description: Params passed to the component's script as the `params` global. Shape defined by the component's params_schema. Server-recognized keys ride here too: `form_reset:true` drops the mount's persisted form_state on this render (use when supplying fresh prefills); `routing:"none"`/`"auto"` overrides activity routing as in `render`.

id.description: Stable mount id (replace-in-place). Reserved shell element ids ("main", "topbar", "status", "overlay", …) are refused with {ok:false, reserved:true}, exactly as in `render`.

force.description: Take over a pane owned by another writer (owner:"service:<name>" or "pane:<id>"). Without it, mounting over an owned pane soft-rejects with {ok:false, owned:true, owner}.

after.description: Position in the page sequence: place the pane right after this pane/markdown id, or "start" for the top. Omitted: a new pane appends and a re-render keeps its position. An unknown id still mounts (appended) and returns a `warning`. Pair with `write_markdown` to put headings and prose between runs of panes.

place.description: Proposed grid placement on the page's 12-column grid: `col` (1–12, the column it starts in; omit for auto flow), `span` (2–12 columns wide, shrunk to fit right of `col`; default the rest of the row), `rows` (2–24 rows of 40px; omit for auto height). Out-of-range values are clamped and the applied placement comes back as `place`. It also becomes this pane's "Claude's layout" baseline — the user can rearrange freely and ↺ puts the run back. Omitted: a new pane is full-width auto-height and a re-render keeps whatever layout the user left.

signals.description: Optional declared wake signals (channels), exactly as in `render`: each entry names a store key this pane writes on a deliberate user action and how it should wake you. wake:"queue" (default) folds a browser write to that key into the user's queue rail, to send when they hit Push; wake:"immediate" wakes you the moment the pane writes it.

key.description: The store key the pane writes (e.g. "form_submit").

why.description: Short human label for why this wakes you (shown in the queue rail).

keys.description: Specific store keys to read. Omit to fetch everything.

patch.description: Object whose keys+values are merged into the store.

since.description: Only return events with seq > this. Default 0 (all).

a.description: First node: hierarchical label (n1.2), opaque id (n3), `active`, or `live`.

context.description: Context lines around each html diff hunk. Default 2.

since.description: Only return pins with seq greater than this (exclusive). Pass the prior call's next_cursor to get just new/edited pins.

mount.description: Scope to pins anchored in this mount id only.

type.description: The element type to read: 'comment' (the default) or 'highlight'.

id.description: The comment pin id (from get_comments, e.g. "c3").

text.description: Your reply. Short and specific — a doc comment, not an essay.

node.description: A committed node id (e.g. 'n5') to read that node's captures instead of the live surface.

since.description: Only return captures with seq greater than this (catch-up cursor).

capture_id.description: The capture id (e.g. 'cap3'), from get_captures or the tab_capture store key.

selector.description: CSS selector; returns matching elements (tag, text, html), capped.

query.description: Text to find; returns occurrences with surrounding context windows.

profile.description: Re-run a named profile over the raw DOM (e.g. tables). The re-run gets the capture's own URL, so url-derived fields resolve exactly as they did at ingest.

context.description: Chars of context around each query hit (default 200).

target.description: For scope "node": the node's stored id. For scope "pane": the mount id. Omit for "global".

tokens.description: Partial map of --wc-* token → CSS value. Unset tokens fall through the cascade.

css.description: Raw CSS escape hatch. Global/node = chrome only; pane = that pane's content only.

modes.description: Optional per-mode layers { light?: {tokens, css?}, dark?: {tokens, css?} } applied over `tokens`/`css` in that mode.

clear.description: Remove the theme at this scope (ignores tokens/css).

scope.description: Which layer to resolve. Defaults to "global".

mode.description: Which mode to resolve. Defaults to light.

name.description: Theme name (letters, digits, space, dot, dash; becomes <name>.json).

location.description: local = this project; system = ~/.web-chat (all projects). Defaults to local.

tokens.description: Partial map of --wc-* token → CSS value.

css.description: Optional raw-CSS escape hatch baked into the saved theme.

modes.description: Optional per-mode layers { light?: {tokens, css?}, dark?: {tokens, css?} } — see set_theme.

set_default.description: Also set this as the web-chat-wide default at the chosen location.

scope.description: Which layer to apply it at.

format.description: 'html' (default): one page. 'replay': the lineage as a self-contained .html player. 'gif': the lineage as an animated GIF. 'mp4' (H.264) / 'webm' (VP9): the lineage as a video — needs ffmpeg on the machine.

node.description: For 'html': which node to export — a hierarchical label ('n1.7'), a stored id, 'active' (default), or 'live'. For a replay format it means the same as `to`.

from.description: Replay formats: the node to start from (label or id). Default: the nearest bookmarked ancestor of `to`, else its root.

to.description: Replay formats: the node to arrive at (label or id). Default: the active node.

hold_ms.description: Replay formats: how long each node is held, in ms (500–20000, default 2500).

captions.description: Replay formats: 'on' (default) — a caption per node: its label, time and Claude's reply summary (plus the prompt when include_prompts is true) — or 'none' for no caption bar.

include_prompts.description: Replay formats: true puts the user's own prompts in the captions (they may be private). Default false: no prompt text anywhere in the file.

width.description: 'gif'/'mp4'/'webm': output width in px (320–1920, default 960); the height follows `size` (16:10 by default), and a frame of more than 1920 by 1200 px in area shrinks to fit, keeping its shape. The result gives the width and height drawn.

fps.description: 'gif'/'mp4'/'webm': frames per second for motion — a fade, and the scroll to each change — and a video's frame rate (1–30, default 10). Left out, a replay too long for the 1000-frame cap is drawn at the highest fps that fits; a named fps is kept, and a replay over the cap at it is refused.

size.description: Replay formats: the page size each frame is laid out at, 'WxH' in CSS px — digits and a lowercase x, e.g. '1280x800' (the default); a width beyond 320–3840 or a height beyond 240–2160 is clamped, and any other form is refused. It also gives a GIF or video its shape; a width of 900 or less lays the page out as a narrow screen does.

mode.description: Draw the file in this light/dark mode of the theme. Default: light, whatever the user's browser shows — pass 'dark' only when the user asks for a dark copy.

script.description: A replay SCRIPT (see above): the two moments and, optionally, timed and captioned beats between them. Replaces `from`/`to` (a top-level from/to/include_prompts fills in what the script leaves out).

from.description: The first moment: a node label or id, an ancestor of `to`. Default: the nearest bookmarked ancestor, else the root.

to.description: The last moment: a node label or id. Default: the active node.

title.description: A title shown over the captions and naming the document (≤120 chars).

default_hold_ms.description: Hold for steps that set none (500–20000; default 2500).

include_prompts.description: Put the user's own prompts in the captions. Default false.

steps.description: The beats, in path order. Omit to play every node on the path at the default hold.

node.description: One node (label or id) — this beat shows it.

nodes.description: A group of CONSECUTIVE nodes played as one beat: shows the last, the caption lists them all.

hold_ms.description: How long this beat is held (500–20000 ms).

caption.description: A short caption for this beat (≤280 chars).

scroll.description: Where the frame looks during this beat: 'auto' (default — scroll to what the node added, then what it changed), 'none' (hold still), or the id of one pane or markdown item on the node's page.

open.description: true: open the replay (the `script`, or from/to) in the user's browser player instead of writing a file — nothing is written and `format` is ignored.

text.description: The markdown. `#`/`##` headings become entries in the page's Contents nav (`###` is a sub-heading with no row); the first `#` is the page title.

id.description: Stable item id — reuse to replace in place. Omitted: the server assigns md-<n>. Must not be a pane's id or a reserved shell element id.

after.description: Place the item right after this pane/markdown id, or "start" for the top. Omitted: a new item appends; a replaced item keeps its position.

force.description: Replace an item another writer (owner:"service:<name>") owns. Without it, that write soft-rejects with {ok:false, owned:true, owner}.
